coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Genentech Hall
record.summary: UCSF's first Mission Bay building and the first structure completed on the 303-acre campus, opened January 2003 at 600 16th St, housing the biochemistry, biophysics and structural biology programs.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint, not a hand trace or plan estimate. This is the opposite situation from Mission Bay's condo-mapped residential towers (Avalon, Radiance, etc.): here, ONE large Assessor land parcel spans SEVERAL UCSF buildings (confirmed against data/raw/parcels.geojson and DataSF's Assessor tax roll -- e.g. blklot 8711507 at 675 Nelson Rising Lane alone is ~13 acres, far larger than any single building on it), so using the parcel boundary per building would make multiple records overlap and double-count the same ground. The real building footprint is the only non-overlapping, honest shape for each one.

facts.value: Biochemistry, biophysics and structural biology research

costs.what: Total capital-improvement budget the UC Regents amended and approved in March 1999 for 'UC Hall Seismic Replacement, Mission Bay' (Building 24) -- believed to be this building based on matching gross square footage (433,828 gsf) and programs, per the January 2000 Regents item that recounts the March 1999 action; the March 1999 item itself does not use the 'Genentech Hall' name

milestones.text: UC Regents approve an amended $222.4 million capital-improvement budget, funding plan, environmental documentation and design for the 'UC Hall Seismic Replacement, Mission Bay' project (Building 24) -- believed to be this building based on matching gross square footage (433,828 gsf) and programs (structural/chemical biology, molecular/cell/developmental biology), per a January 2000 Regents item recounting the March 1999 action; site preparation began October 1999 and steel-frame construction began December 1999, per the same January 2000 item

open_questions: Exact opening day is sourced only to a first-researcher-moved-in anecdote (Jan 8, 2003) and a February 2003 trade-press 'now open' piece, not an official UCSF dedication date -- recorded as month-level, approximate.
Square footage varies 400,000-435,000 sq ft across sources; not resolved to one authoritative figure.
No openly licensed image was found; none is hosted here.

Images: the only photograph found of Genentech Hall is undated beyond appearing in a September 2008 UC Regents presentation slide (shared with its neighbor); its exact capture date isn't confirmed. No site plan or architectural rendering specific to this building was found in a public-record source.

2026-09-21 pass: identified the March 1999 Regents budget/design approval for 'UC Hall Seismic Replacement, Mission Bay (Building 24)' as this building's likely earlier stage, via a January 2000 Regents item that recounts it and gives 433,828 gsf (matching this record's own 400,000-435,000 range). The March 1999 item itself was not retrieved directly in this pass; the January 2000 item's own recap is the source used.

record.notes: OCII plan block 24A/B. UCSF's first Mission Bay building and the first structure completed on the 303-acre campus. ~400,000-435,000 sq ft (sources vary), five stories. Architect SmithGroup (SF office). Opened January 2003 (a Jan 8, 2003 first-researcher-moved-in anecdote and a Feb 2003 trade-press "now open" piece support the month; not an official UCSF dedication-date citation).
